project.name: osgi/runtime/jgiven-wrap
project.description: jgiven-core + jgiven-junit5 (2.0.3) wrapped as a first-class OSGi bundle — the single jGiven-in-OSGi carrier, living beside scenario-engine in the runtime world (jGiven is a permanent choice, part of the runtime of the playable). Kept a SEPARATE bundle rather than folded into scenario-engine: scenario-engine is already dual-realm (its base package host-flat, its .container package in-container), and merging jGiven's export would force jGiven's whole tail (guava, gson, jakarta.annotation…) into every world that installs scenario-engine — even runner-only ones. A single-responsibility wrap avoids that entanglement. EVERY jgiven dependency already carries a Bundle-SymbolicName (guava, gson, paranamer, jansi, jakarta.annotation, byte-buddy) and slf4j is owned by pax-logging — so there is no not-designed-for-OSGi tail to embed. The wrap is maximally LOCAL: stamp OSGi headers onto the only two header-less jars (the jgiven pair), export com.tngtech.jgiven.*, and Import-Package everything else so each dependency installs as its own pre-existing bundle.
